name: Defense, drones and reshoring
thesis: Western defense spending is in a multi year step up: the US FY2027 request is $1.5 trillion including $350 billion via reconciliation, and NATO allies committed to 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core). The 2025 to 2026 conflicts burned interceptors faster than production lines could replace them, so the money is flowing first to munitions, missile defense, solid rocket motors and cheap mass (drones and counter drone). The constraint is industrial capacity, not budgets, which favors suppliers of chokepoint components (rocket motors, seekers, energetics, shipyard capacity) and the contractors building new plants. Reshoring of chips and defense production adds a parallel construction and automation wave, though CHIPS fab timelines have slipped. The government is also becoming an owner (Intel 9.9%, L3Harris Missile Solutions preferred), which reduces downside for chosen champions but adds policy risk.

facts: July 2026: Army raised the ceiling of Lockheed's PAC-3 production contract to $58.62 billion via a $53.86 billion modification, supporting a FY2026 to FY2032 multiyear procurement (terms not yet definitized).
Lockheed said the funding lets it triple PAC-3 MSE capacity by end of 2030 and grow Camden, Arkansas jobs by 50%; it previously announced a path to 2,000 PAC-3 interceptors per year.
Lockheed is investing $8 billion to $9 billion through 2030 to modernize more than 20 US facilities.
Lockheed won $1.1 billion of SDA Tranche 3 tracking layer awards (18 satellites), the largest of four $3.5 billion total awards.

pipeline.product: FY2027 defense appropriations and second reconciliation bill
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Base request $1.15 trillion plus $350 billion reconciliation. Golden Dome gets $17.5 billion only if reconciliation passes ($400 million in base). Failure of reconciliation would hit missile defense and space names.

pipeline.timing: First 30,000 one way attack drone orders in 2026, deliveries over five months; over 200,000 drones by 2027
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: $1 billion for about 340,000 small drones over two years; 25 vendors in phase one. Rewards low cost, high volume makers and component suppliers (motors, batteries, cameras, radios).

pipeline.product: PAC-3 multiyear definitization and Boeing seeker tripling
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Locks in demand for seekers (Boeing), solid rocket motors (Aerojet within L3Harris, Northrop as second source from August 2026), and energetics.

pipeline.timing: FF(X) launch target 2028; Ingalls got $283 million lead yard contract
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Frigate based on Legend class cutter design; second yard likely needed. Hanwha Philly Shipyard ($5 billion investment) positioned for hull blocks and modules.

pipeline.timing: Reported for 2026, target valuation reported from $1.5 trillion to above $2 trillion (unverified final terms)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Would re-rate listed space peers and give a public benchmark for launch and satellite economics.

pipeline.timing: 3nm equipment installation from Q3 2026, volume production 2027
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Orders for semiconductor equipment and fab construction contractors in the US.

pipeline.product: NATO national plans to reach 3.5% core spending
pipeline.timing: Germany targets 3.5% by 2029 (about EUR 152.8 billion); NATO review in 2029
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: European primes (Rheinmetall backlog expected to approach EUR 135 billion by end 2026) and US exporters of air defense benefit.

layers.name: Energetics, propellants and solid rocket motors
layers.why: Every missile and interceptor needs a rocket motor and explosives, and US supply shrank to two motor makers by 2017.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Two incumbent suppliers; DoD put $1 billion convertible preferred into L3Harris Missile Solutions in April 2026 and Northrop became a second PAC-3 motor source in August 2026. New entrants are scaling.

companies.name: L3Harris Technologies
companies.role: Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, space sensors, communications
companies.note: DoD holds $1 billion convertible preferred in Missile Solutions unit; also $843 million SDA Tranche 3 award.

companies.name: Northrop Grumman
companies.role: Solid rocket motors, B-21, Sentinel, space
companies.note: Second source for PAC-3 MSE motors from August 2026; $784 million SDA Tranche 3.

companies.name: Anduril Industries
companies.role: Solid rocket motors, Roadrunner, autonomous systems
companies.note: Mississippi plant targets 6,000 tactical motors per year by end 2026; Army enterprise contract ceiling $20 billion (March 2026). Private.

companies.name: Olin
companies.role: Winchester ammunition, operates Lake City Army Ammunition Plant
companies.note: Mostly chlor alkali chemicals.

companies.name: Karman Holdings
companies.role: Missile and space subsystems
companies.note: Specific programs unverified.

layers.name: Missiles, munitions and air defense primes
layers.why: Interceptor stockpiles were drawn down in 2025 and 2026, so multiyear munitions contracts are the most certain spending.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Production lines take years to expand; seekers, motors and microelectronics gate output.

companies.name: Lockheed Martin
companies.role: PAC-3 MSE, THAAD, GMLRS, PrSM, JASSM, F-35
companies.note: PAC-3 ceiling $58.62 billion; tripling capacity by 2030.

companies.name: RTX
companies.role: Patriot radar and GEM-T, SM-3/SM-6, Coyote counter drone interceptor
companies.note: Also commercial aerospace (Pratt, Collins).

companies.name: General Dynamics
companies.role: 155mm artillery shell production (OTS), submarines (Electric Boat), combat vehicles
companies.note: 155mm ramp figures not verified in this research.

companies.name: Boeing
companies.role: PAC-3 seekers, defense aircraft
companies.note: Pentagon and Boeing plan to triple PAC-3 seeker production (April 2026). On Oct 5, 2026 Boeing announced an undefinitized seven year contract action from Lockheed worth about $14.7 billion to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker output; some terms are still open. Its Compact Laser Weapon System was picked for the counter drone directed energy pilot (Oct 5, 2026).

companies.name: Rheinmetall
companies.role: European ammunition, vehicles, air defense
companies.note: US OTC RNMBY. Backlog EUR 63.8 billion at end 2025, management expects about EUR 135 billion by end 2026.

companies.name: BAE Systems
companies.role: Munitions, combat vehicles, submarines, electronics
companies.note: US OTC BAESY.

companies.name: Kongsberg Gruppen
companies.role: NASAMS air defense and naval strike missile
companies.note: US OTC NSKFF.

companies.name: Hanwha Aerospace
companies.role: K9 howitzers, ammunition, Hanwha Ocean parent
companies.note: Korea listing.

layers.name: Drones and counter drone
layers.why: Ukraine and Middle East conflicts proved cheap drones in mass, and the defense against them is now an urgent buy.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Airframes are easy to build; Chinese free components (motors, magnets, batteries, cameras) and jam resistant navigation are the real constraint.

companies.name: AeroVironment
companies.role: Switchblade loitering munitions, Puma, BlueHalo counter drone and space
companies.note: Acquired BlueHalo in 2025. Its palletized high energy laser was one of four systems picked for the Pentagon's counter drone directed energy pilot at US bases (Oct 5, 2026); a shoot off is planned for December.

companies.name: Kratos Defense and Security
companies.role: Jet powered target and combat drones (Valkyrie), hypersonics, rocket motors
companies.note: High multiple, high implied volatility.

companies.name: Red Cat Holdings
companies.role: Small reconnaissance drones (Teal Black Widow) for Army SRR
companies.note: Small cap; Drone Dominance award status unverified.

companies.name: Ondas Holdings
companies.role: Autonomous drones and counter drone (Iron Drone)
companies.note: Speculative small cap.

companies.name: Unusual Machines
companies.role: US made drone components (motors, controllers)
companies.note: Component play on NDAA compliant drones; speculative.

companies.name: Epirus
companies.role: Leonidas high power microwave counter drone
companies.note: $43.5 million Army contract for two Gen 2 Leonidas units. Private. Picked for the Pentagon counter drone directed energy pilot (Oct 5, 2026).

companies.name: Leonardo DRS
companies.role: Counter UAS sensors and mission equipment, power and propulsion
companies.note: Majority owned by Leonardo.

layers.name: Defense electronics and software
layers.why: Modern weapons are electronics heavy, and AI targeting and command software are new spending lines.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Rad hard chips and specialty microelectronics have limited suppliers.

companies.name: Palantir Technologies
companies.role: Defense data and AI software (Maven, Army enterprise agreement)
companies.note: Very high valuation; high option premiums.

companies.name: Mercury Systems
companies.role: Secure processing subsystems for radar and EW
companies.note: Mid cap defense electronics.

companies.name: Curtiss-Wright
companies.role: Defense electronics and naval nuclear propulsion components
companies.note: Overlaps with AI power theme.

layers.name: Shipbuilding and naval nuclear
layers.why: The Navy needs more submarines and new frigates, and US shipyards are the most capacity constrained part of defense.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Labor shortages and yard capacity limit output; foreign yards (Hanwha) are being brought in.

companies.name: Huntington Ingalls Industries
companies.role: Aircraft carriers, submarines (with GD), destroyers, FF(X) lead yard
companies.note: $283 million FF(X) lead yard support contract.

companies.name: BWX Technologies
companies.role: Sole supplier of naval nuclear reactors
companies.note: Every submarine and carrier needs BWXT reactor components.

companies.name: Hanwha Ocean
companies.role: Owner of Philly Shipyard, Korean naval and commercial shipbuilder
companies.note: $5 billion Philly Shipyard investment cited in Golden Fleet; near term focus on hull blocks.

layers.name: Space and missile warning
layers.why: Golden Dome and proliferated missile tracking satellites are a new multi year spending line, and launch capacity is a gate.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Launch is dominated by SpaceX; satellite buses and sensors have several suppliers.

companies.name: Rocket Lab
companies.role: Electron launch, Neutron in development, satellite builder
companies.note: $805 million SDA Tranche 3 tracking award (18 satellites). Neutron first launch slipped into 2026, possibly 2027 (unverified).

companies.name: Firefly Aerospace
companies.role: Alpha launch vehicle and lunar landers

companies.name: Planet Labs
companies.role: Earth observation satellites and data
companies.note: Defense and intelligence customers.

companies.name: Redwire
companies.role: Space infrastructure and components
companies.note: Small cap.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.role: Dominant launch provider, Starlink, Starshield
companies.note: IPO reported for 2026; not yet tradable as of this writing (verify).

layers.name: Semiconductor reshoring (CHIPS Act fabs) and equipment
layers.why: Leading edge and memory fabs in the US are a national security priority, and they drive tool and construction demand.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Tools and skilled labor are available but timelines slip; Intel Ohio pushed to 2030 to 2031.

companies.name: Intel
companies.role: US leading edge fabs (Arizona Fab 52 on 18A); government owns about 9.9%
companies.note: 433.3 million shares at $20.47 ($8.9 billion) in August 2025.

companies.name: Taiwan Semiconductor
companies.role: Arizona fabs; fab 2 3nm tools installing from Q3 2026
companies.note: Fab 1 producing 4nm for Apple, Nvidia, AMD.

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.role: Boise, Idaho and New York memory fabs
companies.note: Idaho fab timing per company (unverified exact date).

companies.name: Applied Materials
companies.role: Deposition, etch and other fab tools
companies.note: China export restrictions offset US fab demand.

companies.name: Lam Research
companies.role: Etch and deposition tools
companies.note: Memory heavy exposure.

companies.name: ASML
companies.role: Sole supplier of EUV lithography
companies.note: Every leading edge fab needs ASML.

layers.name: Industrial construction and automation
layers.why: New munitions plants, fabs, shipyards and data centers need contractors and factory automation, and labor is the constraint.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Skilled trades are short; contractors have record backlogs.

companies.name: Comfort Systems USA
companies.role: Mechanical and electrical contractor for fabs and data centers
companies.note: Record $14.1 billion backlog at Q2 2026.

companies.name: EMCOR Group
companies.role: Electrical and mechanical construction
companies.note: Fabs, data centers, manufacturing.

companies.name: Rockwell Automation
companies.role: Factory automation and controls
companies.note: Reshoring beneficiary; cyclical.

companies.name: Teradyne
companies.role: Collaborative robots (Universal Robots) and chip test
companies.note: Robotics plus semi test.

second_order.idea: Rare earth magnets and tungsten as defense inputs
second_order.why: US restricts Chinese tungsten in defense procurement from 2027 and drones need magnets; see critical materials theme.

second_order.idea: Government as shareholder of defense chokepoints
second_order.why: DoD preferred in L3Harris Missile Solutions and Treasury stake in Intel signal the state will backstop strategic suppliers.

second_order.idea: Korean shipbuilders as the US Navy's overflow capacity
second_order.why: Hanwha Philly is cited as a Golden Fleet cornerstone; legal limits on foreign built warships remain a hurdle.

second_order.idea: European defense as the cleaner volume story
second_order.why: Germany targets 3.5% of GDP by 2029; NATO 5% by 2035 gives a decade of procurement runway.

second_order.idea: Electrical and mechanical contractors bridge reshoring, defense plants and data centers
second_order.why: Same labor pool serves all three waves.
